Lessons.Title: Tiny House: Design and Solve PLC Activity
ExplanationParagraphs: First Edition 2021 Grade 3 Unit 8 Lesson 4. The public teacher original has a notice-and-wonder warm-up (10 minutes), tiny-house design (25 minutes), Ask, Revise, and Answer (15 minutes), synthesis and a gated five-minute assessment. Source activity statements, three footprint dimension options and their dimensions are verified against the authorized locally saved 2021 HTML. Original photos, diagrams, a separate PDF and publisher-gated Cool-down are not visually certified. Publisher images are linked, never copied.

Warm-up Notice and Wonder: Tiny Houses. In pairs, inspect the original tiny-house pictures with the teacher and discuss size, area, advantages and trade-offs. The source pictures show different real-life tiny-house types. Questions and visual details need teacher assessment; a numerical-only answer cannot certify the original warm-up.

Activity 1 Design a Tiny House. Choose ONE of three original designs. Option shipping container: rectangular single floor 8 feet by 20 feet = 160 square feet, perimeter 56 feet. Option cabin: downstairs rectangle 8 by 10 feet = 80 square feet; upstairs 8 by 8 feet = 64 square feet. Total combined floor area across levels is 144 square feet, not the area of one floor. The downstairs boundary perimeter is 36 feet and upstairs 32 feet; do not falsely report a single 144-square-foot exterior perimeter for both levels. Option school bus: floor 7 by 14 feet = 98 square feet, perimeter 42 feet for an idealized rectangular floor.

The 2021 source asks pupils to partition their chosen shape into rooms and depict doors, windows, furniture and any essential details. Students may work alone, with partners or in groups up to four. Their partition plan and space allocation are individually generated and not copied from a publisher visual. Room-areas must sum to the correct floor area on each level; each square-foot region is disjoint and correctly labelled.

Activity 2 Ask, Revise, and Answer: based on the student own drawing, independently WRITE TWO questions: one about area and one about perimeter. First answer and improve your questions with one partner, then swap designs and solve questions with a NEW partner. Not every learner design has a unique numerical answer. Teacher checks whether questions are solvable from the indicated room or outer boundary, and checks feet vs square feet.

Independent Edulytics worked example: shipping container area 20 × 8 = 160 square feet, perimeter 2 × (20 + 8) = 56 feet. School bus 14 × 7 = 98 square feet, perimeter 42 feet. Cabin total two-floor area 8 × 10 + 8 × 8 = 144 square feet across both stories. Do not misinterpret the combined cabin area as an exterior 2D perimeter or as a ground footprint.

At synthesis, students display designs, share their area and perimeter questions, discuss alternative room plans and respond to peer revisions. Preserve original physical collaboration, floor-plan reasoning, and dialogue. Only an independent, separate Edulytics Cool-down may be offered; original restricted source Cool-down is not copied. Runtime tests and Stage D remain deferred.

KeyConcepts.Title: Area and perimeter units
KeyConcepts.Definition: Area counts square units inside a flat region; perimeter counts one-dimensional units along the boundary.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use square feet for area, feet for perimeter.

KeyConcepts.Title: Two-story floor area
KeyConcepts.Definition: The cabin has 80 ft² downstairs plus 64 ft² upstairs.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Add floor areas only for total usable area; do not claim one combined exterior perimeter without defining the boundary.
KeyConcepts.Example: Cabin 144 ft² total over two levels.

KeyConcepts.Title: Partition without overlap
KeyConcepts.Definition: Room areas subdivide the available rectangular floor plan.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Sum of disjoint room areas equals the original rectangular floor area.
KeyConcepts.Example: A 20 × 8 container can include 2 rooms of 10 × 8 each, total 160 ft².

WorkedExamples.Title: Rectangular container
WorkedExamples.Question: Find the area and perimeter of a shipping-container floor of width 8 ft and length 20 ft.
WorkedExamples.Method: Area = length × width; perimeter = twice their sum.
Steps: Partition 160 square feet among rooms with no overlaps.

WorkedExamples.Title: Two-story cabin
WorkedExamples.Question: Find the combined floor area of a cabin with 8 × 10 ft downstairs and 8 × 8 ft upstairs.
WorkedExamples.Method: Compute area for each story and add.
Steps: Total across two stories = 144 square feet.
WorkedExamples.Answer: 144 ft² total area; separate perimeters 36 ft downstairs and 32 ft upstairs.
WorkedExamples.Check: Do not combine two story perimeters as a unique outline.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat the cabin 144 ft² as one rectangular footprint.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 80 and 64 square feet are different stories.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Keep stories separate and sum areas only when asking total floor area.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Count both room divider lengths as outside boundary.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Perimeter is the selected outer boundary, not the sum of all interior walls.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Specify whether the question is about a room outline or building exterior.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Label area in ft rather than ft².
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Area and perimeter measure different dimensions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Write square feet for area and feet for boundary length.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Auto-grade drawings or partner-made questions by a single fixed answer.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source activity allows different valid room partitions and peer-generated questions.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Require accurate diagrams and teacher-reviewed explanations.

SummaryPoints: Source choices: container 8×20 (160 ft²), cabin 8×10 downstairs and 8×8 upstairs (144 ft² total), bus 7×14 (98 ft²).
Design rooms, windows, door and furniture; respect level-specific areas.
Ask one area and one perimeter question; revise with partner, answer with a new partner.
Teacher reviews open original image-and-design work. Source graphics, student PDF and gated Cool-down are not copied.
